rationale: Retire the read-side tolerance in setRenderContextScalarsFromData — the second `if`, which adopts a renamed key's TEMPLATE spelling (`current_page`) as a string fallback when the step-boundary name (`current_page_name`) is absent from the map being merged. This is the separable follow-up the step-5 flip commit (5fe010ada, corr 26186633) deliberately left out, and that round accepted the separation provided the nil behaviour was described; this submission carries that description and the retirement's own grounds. THE ORIGINAL JUSTIFICATION IS NOT USED AND IS EXPLICITLY DISAVOWED IN THE NEW COMMENT: the code's own retire-me note argued from ~24h orchestration_states retention, which is unsound twice over — that table holds rows back to 2026-07-19 (retention is per-status, not a day), and the tolerance's second live input is stored page_components.content_data, which never expires. The sound grounds, all MEASURED fresh today (2026-08-21 ~19:4xZ), none argued from memory: (1) ZERO non-terminal orchestrations created before the rename roll (v1.0.1317, both pods up 2026-08-19 22:26Z) — checked against the full 7-status vocabulary (AWAITING_RESPONSES/EXECUTING_STEP/INITIALIZED/RUNNING all zero pre-roll), so no restorable tree written by the old binary exists; every post-roll tree is written by renderCtxToMap, which emits the step name and (pinned by test) never the old one. (2) On the rerender path, buildRerenderBaseData writes `current_page_name` fresh from its pageName argument (rerender_page_sections_action.go:1200-1201), and the only remaining inputs that could reach the fallback — live page_components rows whose stored content_data carries `current_page` as a string — number 18 across 11 sites and ALL 18 agree exactly with their page's own name (regexp_replace(p.name,'\.html$','') join; differ_from_page = 0). So the fallback's entire live input population supplies a value the base merge already set: retirement changes the resolved value on ZERO live rows. (3) Behaviour on absence, as the flip round asked: the loop does data[key].(string) and acts only on ok && s != ""; a missing key, nil, or non-string all give ok=false and the struct field is left at its PRIOR value — no panic, no empty overwrite, no new blank. Beyond removing dead weight, retirement closes a door the tolerance held open: the rerender path merges base, then stored contentData, then resolved_data as three separate calls, and the tolerance operates per-call — so a stored map carrying an old-key string with no step name in THAT map would today clobber the fresh page identity set by the base merge (bugs_closed/085's exact shape: page renders another page's identity; note 085 IS in bugs_closed at HEAD — `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- bugs_open/ bugs_closed/ | grep 085_` returns exactly one line, bugs_closed/085_HANDOFF_2026-07-26_..., moved by 916c8b22b — if a seat's case index lists it as open, the index predates 2026-08-19). Today 18/18 stored strings agree so the clobber is latent, but nothing prevents a future writer storing a stale one; after retirement the stale-clobber is unrepresentable through this seam. Template-visible behaviour is UNCHANGED in both directions on all 18 rows for a second, independent reason: mergeIntoRenderContext's catch-all copies every merged key into ctx.ContentData, and contextToInterfaceMap merges ContentData over the derived scalars, so {{.current_page}} on those rows is supplied by ContentData regardless of the struct field. The delta is confined to the struct field itself — i.e. the step output renderCtxToMap emits and Go readers of ctx.CurrentPage. Verification: mutation-proved — restoring the tolerance in a git-archive-HEAD copy fails exactly the new 'old key alone is NOT adopted' pin and nothing else; removing it returns green; the pin cannot pass vacuously because case 1 (step name resolves) shares the same map shape. Full ./platform/... green in the clean archive copy carrying only these two files.

plan.risks: Go change, inert until an image builds from a HEAD containing it and rolls — it will ride whatever roll carries the flip or the next fleet roll, and needs no ordering relative to the flip (the flip round's own interim-window analysis established the tolerance is inert with respect to the flip in both directions; this removal keeps that true trivially). Residual risk is a caller OUTSIDE the measured population hand-building a context map under the old spelling and relying on adoption: the fleet grep found no Go site doing so (the only remaining `current_page`-as-string writers are the 18 stored rows, measured), and any such future caller now gets the same treatment the page RECORD always got — ignored, field keeps its prior value — rather than a silent adoption. The 18 stored rows will drift stale over time by design; they are input to ContentData only, which is unchanged.
